transcript:
User: I want to be upfront: the last marketing agency strung me along for three months and I got nothing. Why would you be different?
Agent: Yeah, I hear you — three months of waiting and nothing to show for it would make anyone skeptical.  

So I don’t repeat their mistakes: what specifically did they promise you and fail to deliver — more calls, better follow-up, appointments, something else?
User: They promised more patient bookings and better call handling, but once I signed up, they disappeared.
Agent: Got it, so they talked a big game about more patient bookings and better call handling, then basically ghosted you once you were in.  

When you think back on those three months, did you actually notice *any* change in how your calls were handled or how many patients got booked, or was it literally business as usual the whole time?
User: It was business as usual. No noticeable changes, just empty promises once they had my card details.
Agent: Yeah, that makes sense — once someone’s taken your card and nothing changes, it’s hard to trust the next pitch.  

So instead of vague promises, let’s be specific: on a typical day at your practice, what actually happens when a patient calls and no one can grab the phone right away — does it ring out, go to voicemail, or bounce around the front desk?
User: Calls usually go to voicemail, and we try to return them, but it's not always immediate.
Agent: Mhm, I hear you — so most calls hit voicemail and you’re circling back when you can, but there’s a lag.  

When someone calls with, say, a toothache or something urgent and it goes to voicemail, do you feel like they usually wait for your call back, or are you worried they just ring the next dentist who picks up?
User: Honestly, I worry they call the next available dentist and we lose potential patients.
Agent: Yeah, that’s exactly the gap we focus on — stopping those urgent callers from drifting to the next dentist just because no one picked up.  

So roughly how many calls a week would you say are going to voicemail instead of being answered live?
User: We miss about 18 calls a week, and it's frustrating because most of those could have been bookings.
Agent: Got it, 18 a week is a lot of chances to help patients just slipping through.  

Has anyone ever walked you through what those missed calls are actually costing you in lost revenue, or has it mostly just been a gut feeling so far?
User: Mostly a gut feeling. I know we lose out on revenue, but no one's given me concrete numbers before.
Agent: Makes sense, most folks are just guessing on this stuff.  

Mind if we put some real numbers to it together—just a quick ballpark—so you can actually see what those missed calls are worth?
User: Sure, I'm open to seeing what those missed calls could mean in terms of actual revenue.
Agent: Nice, that helps.  

So ballpark for your practice—of those 18 missed calls a week, what percentage do you think would’ve actually booked an appointment if someone had picked up right away: maybe 40–50%, or higher?
User: I'd say around 60% would have booked if someone picked up immediately.
Agent: Got it, so most of those missed callers were pretty serious about booking.  

And for a typical new patient appointment—say an exam plus whatever’s usually done on that first visit—about how much revenue does that bring in on average?
User: An average visit brings in about $240. That's why missing those calls really stings financially.
Agent: Yeah… that adds up fast.  

Just using your numbers, those 18 missed calls with 60% likely to book at $240 each is about $2,591 walking out the door every week when it rings to voicemail instead of a live answer.  

If there were a way to hand a big chunk of that $2,591 back to you every week by making sure those calls get answered and booked, would you actually want to see how that could work, or are you feeling too burned from the last agency to even go there right now?
User: I'm cautious. What happens after I sign? Will I get dropped once you have my card?
Agent: Totally fair question — you got burned once, you don’t want a repeat. After you sign, it’s the opposite of “disappear”: Jay walks you through a short setup, we turn the system on, then we watch your missed calls together and track how many turn into booked patients, so you can see it working in real numbers, not promises.  

So… to actually show you that and walk through your $11,200/month leak on a screen, would you be open to a quick 20‑minute walkthrough with Jay this week?
User: Okay... one demo. But I'm watching closely. Let's schedule that walkthrough.
Agent: Love it — one demo, under the microscope, that’s fair.  

First thing I need so we can lock this in for you: what’s your first name?
User: Bianca. I want this scheduled in Mountain/Phoenix time, please. Let's see what you've got.
Agent: Nice, thanks Bianca — and got it on Mountain/Phoenix time.  

And what’s your last name, so I put this under the right profile for Jay?
User: Cole. It's Bianca Cole. Let's get this right, please.
Agent: Got it, Bianca Cole — thanks for spelling that out.  

And what’s the name of your practice so we book this under the right company?
User: It's Cole Family Dental in Phoenix. Please ensure all details reflect Mountain/Phoenix time for our demo.
Agent: Perfect, Cole Family Dental in Phoenix — and yes, we’ll keep everything in Mountain/Phoenix time.  

Quick check, Bianca: is the number you’re calling from the best one to text your demo confirmation to?
User: Yes, please use this number for the demo confirmation. Thank you for accommodating the Mountain/Phoenix time.
Agent: Perfect, we’ll use this number and keep everything in Mountain time.  

One moment while I check availability—would you prefer later today or tomorrow for the demo?
Agent: Got it, we’ll keep texting and timing all in Mountain for you.  

For the walkthrough with Jay, do you want to do that later today or tomorrow?
User: Tomorrow works better. Can you do afternoon in Mountain/Phoenix time?
Agent: Perfect, tomorrow afternoon in Mountain works.  

I can get you in tomorrow at either 12:00 or 12:45 in the afternoon Mountain time — which works better for you?
User: 12:45 PM Mountain/Phoenix time works for me. Let's go with that. Thank you.
Agent: One moment while I confirm that on the calendar for you.
Agent: Bianca, you’re all set — Jay will meet with you tomorrow at 12:45 PM Mountain/Phoenix time, and you’ll get a text in a moment with the confirmation and a link in case you need to reschedule. Is there anything else you want to make sure we cover on that call, or are you good for now?
